classification.difficultyReason: Apply the sine rule and select the obtuse supplement of the calculator's acute angle.

content.prompt: Given that $\theta$ is an obtuse angle, find its value, correct to the nearest degree.

spec.description: Low triangle with horizontal base, upper obtuse vertex and all supplied labels. Ordinary source-blue outlines become house black.
spec.mathematics: The base is 15 cm, opposite the upper angle theta. The left base angle is 20 degrees, opposite the right sloping side of length 8 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and theta are visible; no calculated angle is shown.

answer.worked:
By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{15}&=\frac{\sin20^\circ}{8}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{15\sin20^\circ}{8}.\end{align*}$$
Since $\theta$ is obtuse, take the supplement of the acute inverse-sine value:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{15\sin20^\circ}{8}\right)\\\theta&\approx140^\circ.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Oblique triangle with left vertex, lower-right obtuse vertex and upper-right acute vertex. Ordinary source-blue outlines become house black.
spec.mathematics: The side from the left vertex to the upper-right vertex is 13 m and is opposite theta. The side from the left vertex to the lower-right vertex is 9 m and is opposite the supplied upper-right angle of 17 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements and theta are visible; no calculated angle is shown.

answer.worked:
By the sine rule,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{13}&=\frac{\sin17^\circ}{9}\\\sin\theta&=\frac{13\sin17^\circ}{9}.\end{align*}$$
Since $\theta$ is obtuse, take the supplement of the acute inverse-sine value:
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{13\sin17^\circ}{9}\right)\\\theta&\approx155^\circ.\end{align*}$$
